findings.description: MergeLockLostError is an Error subclass declared inline in merge-gate.service.ts, next to withMergeLock which throws it, instead of in merge-gate.errors.ts beside MergeLockHeldError (general.md §Code layout: no inline error classes).
findings.body:
**Rule: `docs/conventions/general.md` §Code layout, no inline error classes.** The rule reads: *"No inline error classes. An `Error` subclass is declared in the area's `errors/` folder, never beside the code that throws it."*

This PR adds `MergeLockLostError` to `merge-gate.service.ts`, right next to `withMergeLock`, which throws it:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/2b7d642056d2ef42b9bb5862deec993fd46c5edb/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L911-L930

The merge-gate area already keeps its errors separate. `src/core/merge-gate.errors.ts` holds `MergeLockHeldError` and `SessionNotReviewableError`, and the service imports both from it. Because the new lock error lives in a different place, `src/cli/index.ts` now imports `MergeLockLostError` from the service module and `MergeLockHeldError` from the errors file.

**Fix:** move the class and its JSDoc into `src/core/merge-gate.errors.ts`. That file imports only a type from `db.client.js`, so the move creates no import cycle. Then update the imports in `merge-gate.service.ts`, `src/cli/index.ts` and the tests.

findings.description: steerSession pastes the message before it writes the steer event, so if the store write then fails (SQLITE_BUSY after the 5 s busy timeout, or a full disk), a peer that did get the message is listed as unsteered and the operator is told to steer it again, which sends the message twice.

ADR 0132 still says the `landed` event is "the lock's last write". This PR moves the steer and the audit under the lock after that event, as amended 0088 now says, so reword it, e.g. "The `landed` event is written before the steer and the audit, so…".

The release renames whatever is at the lock path before checking that it is the take's own directory. If a session moves run A's lock and run B takes a fresh one, A's release (now reported as a lost lock) also moves B's live lock aside, so a third run can take the lock while B is still running. Checking directoryIdentity(lockPath) against `taken` before the rename would close this.
